history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the famous Tripura Sundari temple is NOT in Agartala - it stands at Matabari near UDAIPUR, Gomati district, about 55 km from Agartala (documented with the corrected location). DUPLICATE WARNING: this is almost certainly the SAME shrine as CSV row 1026 'Tripura Sundari Temple [Udaipur]' in the next batch - recommend merging into one record; this 1021 record is written with a distinct ID so the coordinator can dedup. One of the 51 Shakti Peethas (right foot/Dakshin Charan of Sati is said to have fallen here; Bhairava Tripuresh); the state of Tripura is named after this temple. Built 1501 CE by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya after a dream-vision, on a tortoise-hump-shaped hillock (Kurma Pitha); Bengali Ek-ratna style, 24 sq ft base, 75 ft height. Two black-stone idols: 5-ft Tripura Sundari and 2-ft Chhoto-Ma (Chandi), the smaller once carried to battlefields by the kings. Kalyan Sagar lake beside the temple shelters rare Bostami turtles (considered extinct in the wild). Redeveloped under the PRASHAD scheme (Rs 34.43 crore), inaugurated 22 September 2025 by PM Modi. Note: animal sacrifice was banned October 2019 and resumed December 2019 after a 57-day ban (Indian Express) - current practice not verified.

name: Tripura Sundari Temple (Matabari, Udaipur)
town: Matabari, Udaipur, Gomati district (CSV town 'Agartala' is WRONG - ~55 km away)
town_description: Udaipur (in Tripura, not Rajasthan) was the ancient capital of the Manikya kingdom in Gomati district. Matabari ('abode of the mother'), about 5 km from Udaipur town on a tortoise-hump hillock, is Tripura's holiest Shakti shrine; the sacred Kalyan Sagar lake lies beside the temple.
